title: Why Is My Dog's Poop Yellow or Gray? When to See a Vet — POOPIEMATE
description: What yellow, gray or white dog poop can mean, from food and fast gut transit to bile, pancreas and parasite problems, and when each one needs a vet.
og_title: Why Is My Dog's Poop Yellow or Gray? When to See a Vet
main:
Yellow or Gray Dog Poop: What It Means and When to See a Vet

Yellow dog poop is often down to food or poop moving through the gut too fast, while gray or white poo can come from a bone-heavy diet or a bile or pancreas problem. If it happens once, keep an eye on it, but if it lasts a few days, looks greasy, or comes with diarrhea or vomiting, talk to your vet.

Why is healthy dog poop brown?

Bile made in the liver changes as it moves through the gut, and that's what turns poop brown. So when bile doesn't mix in well, poop moves through too fast, or food isn't digested properly, the color can change.

Why dog poop turns yellow

CauseWhat happens
Food and treatsIngredients or coloring in the food, or yellow treats (pumpkin, sweet potato and so on), can make poop look yellow.
Fast gut transitWhen poop moves through the gut too fast, bile doesn't have time to turn brown, so it can come out yellow. It often shows up with soft stools or diarrhea.
Liver or bile duct problemsIf yellow poop comes with yellowing eyes or gums, or low energy, the liver or gallbladder may need a check.
Giardia and other parasitesSuspect this when soft, yellow poop with mucus keeps coming back. A stool test confirms it.

Why dog poop turns gray or white

CauseWhat happens
A diet high in bone or calciumA raw diet or lots of bone treats can produce white poop that crumbles like chalk. Constipation often comes with it.
Not enough bileWhen bile doesn't reach the gut properly, poop can turn pale gray or clay-colored.
Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency (EPI)Without enough digestive enzymes, poop comes out grayish, greasy and large in volume, and a dog can lose weight even while eating well.
Fatty stoolWhen fat isn't digested, poop can come out gray, shiny and very smelly.

White, rice-like bits aren't a poop color. They can be worms, so have your vet run a test.

This guide is general reference information, not a diagnosis. If your dog seems tired or unwell, or you're worried about any symptom, talk to your vet.

When to see a vet

  • Go right away: yellow poop with yellowing eyes, gums or skin; vomiting or lethargy along with it; any blood
  • Call soon: gray or clay-colored poop that keeps coming; greasy, large poops together with weight loss
  • Watch a few days, then call: soft, yellow poop that lasts more than 2 to 3 days; white poop and constipation that keep coming back

To check other colors (black, green, bloody) all in one place, use the dog poop color chart. If there's diarrhea too, also see Why dogs get diarrhea.

Frequently Asked Questions

My dog's poop is yellow. Is that okay?

If it's a one-off and your dog is eating and playing normally, it may just be the food or treats. If it lasts a few days, comes with diarrhea or vomiting, or the eyes or gums turn yellow, talk to your vet.

What does gray dog poop mean?

It can mean bile isn't mixing in well, or the pancreas isn't making enough digestive enzymes. If it looks greasy or keeps happening, talk to your vet.

My dog's poop is white and crumbly.

This is common on diets high in bone or calcium. Constipation often comes with it, so cut back on bones and check with your vet.

My dog has yellow diarrhea with mucus.

The gut may be irritated, or it could be a parasite such as giardia. If it keeps coming back, get a stool test.
